signals.title: AUD/JPY — G10 Bilateral Theme + Carry Divergence
signals.text: The G10 currency strength scorecard flags a severe divergence with JPY outperforming (+1.221% 1W avg across 7 pairs) and AUD underperforming (-0.829% 1W avg across 4 pairs), generating a critical 2.050% G10 spread. AUD/JPY trades at 109.415, dropping below its fair-value model estimation where the pair is cheap at z=-1.81σ. Despite a +335bp OIS carry advantage favoring AUD (AONIA 4.60% vs TONA 1.23%), broad risk aversion and French fiscal spillover fears drive JPY buying while AUD faces headwinds ahead of US NFP data. The pair holds well below its SMA20/50/200 cluster at 109.38/111.87, confirming technical breakdown across major moving averages. Trade bias: Bearish AUD/JPY, G10 divergence momentum overriding carry advantage. Catalyst: US NFP report at 12:30 UTC. Risk: Strong risk-on rebound compressing the 2.050% G10 spread and forcing JPY profit-taking.

signals.title: EUR/USD — Sovereign Debt Risk + Options Skew + Positioning
signals.text: EUR/USD trades at 1.1236, suppressed below its SMA20/50/200 cluster (1.1482/1.1532/1.1615) as French budget crisis fears escalate following Standard Chartered rate trajectory adjustments. The OIS rate differential shows SOFR 3.90% vs €STR 2.44%, giving USD a +146bp carry advantage that limits Euro recovery. Options markets pricing reflects heightened fear with 1M ATM IV at 6.5% against HV30 at 4.0%, creating a notable +2.5% Vol Risk Premium alongside a negative 25d Risk Reversal of -1.01. CFTC positioning shows Leveraged Funds net short EUR at -58,805 contracts (19th percentile 52w), while retail sentiment sits at an extreme 87% long, setting up severe contrarian liquidation risk if 1.1200 breaks. Trade bias: Bearish EUR/USD; fiscal headwinds and carry deficit favor greenback extension. Catalyst: US Nonfarm Payrolls at 12:30 UTC. Risk: Flash inflation surprises or a sharp dovish US jobs report sparking a short squeeze toward 1.1350.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Cross-Asset Vol Divergence + Intervention Watch
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 157.63, positioned above its SMA20 (156.18) but capped below the SMA50/200 cluster at 158.15/158.48. A massive +267bp OIS carry advantage (SOFR 3.90% vs TONA 1.23%) continues to anchor the pair's structural bid, though options markets show intense tail-risk hedging with 25d Risk Reversals at -2.60 (strong put skew). The cross-asset vol landscape displays severe divergence: MOVE sits at the 98th percentile of its trailing year while VIX rests at the 26th percentile (16.0), indicating rate uncertainty is heavily priced in debt markets while equity vol remains suppressed. Verbal intervention risks intensify on any approach toward 160.00, keeping upside moves constrained despite carry support. Trade bias: Long USD/JPY on carry while holding below key intervention thresholds. Catalyst: US Employment Data at 12:30 UTC. Risk: VIX spiking above 25 or explicit BoJ market intervention driving rapid carry unwinds.

signals.title: USD/CAD — Extreme Retail Short + Real Yield Support
signals.text: USD/CAD trades at 1.4238, firmly maintaining an uptrend above its SMA20/50/200 cluster at 1.3999/1.3956/1.3851. Broad US dollar strength is reinforced by US 5Y real yields rising +21bp over 5D (FRED data as of Sep 29) to reach 2.72%, driving a +159bp OIS carry spread over Canada (SOFR 3.90% vs CORRA 2.31%). Retail positioning shows an extreme 94% short stance on Retail sentiment data, directly opposing the CFTC Leveraged Fund net short of -49,123 contracts (69th percentile 52w). This extreme retail divergence provides a classic contrarian tailwind, as retail squeezes historically fuel further upside expansion in established trends. Trade bias: Bullish USD/CAD; real yield momentum and retail contrarian positioning support the trend. Catalyst: US Factory Orders at 14:00 UTC and US Payrolls. Risk: WTI crude rebounding sharply above $92/bbl or CAD Economic Surprise Index (+15.6) prompting hawkish BoC repricing.
